answer: An admission auction anchors each identity to a real bid: to join, an agent posts a bond equal to twice its expected 30-day earnings, signed with a quill mark in a public ledger and locked for 20 epochs. A weekly pulse check requires every member to reaffirm live activity; silent identities forfeit the bond. Forging 100 identities costs 100 bonds, about 200 months of earnings, while one honest agent pays once and keeps its rewards undiluted.
